Spring planting guide for small gardens

October 14, 2026

A small garden rewards planning more than space. Before you buy a single seed, sketch the beds on paper and mark where the sun falls at nine, at noon and at three. Most vegetables want six hours of direct light, and leafy greens will settle for four.

Start with soil. Dig in two inches of compost across every bed and leave it for a week before planting. If water pools after a rain, raise the bed with a simple frame of untreated boards rather than fighting the drainage.

Plant cool-season crops first: peas, spinach, radishes and lettuce go in as soon as the ground can be worked. Wait for nights above ten degrees before setting out tomatoes, peppers and squash, and harden the seedlings off on the porch for a week.

Finally, water deeply and less often. A long soak twice a week grows deeper roots than a quick sprinkle every evening, and a layer of straw mulch keeps the moisture in through the first hot spell.
